---
title: "Offshore Wind Infrastructure Model Assumptions"
readiness: context_only
---

This encyclopedia documents the methodology and techno-economic assumptions used to model offshore wind infrastructure, electricity export, offshore hydrogen production, and hydrogen transport.

The site is organised as an assumptions manual. Each component page bundles the modelling choices that matter for that component:

- cost model, including CAPEX, installation cost, O&M, and scaling
- energy balance, including conversion efficiency, auxiliary power, and losses
- availability treatment on an annual energy basis
- sizing, mass, geometry, and other drivers that affect costs elsewhere in the value chain
- source basis, uncertainty, and architecture applicability

The emphasis is deliberately methodological. Results, scenario outcomes, and interpretation of model output are out of scope for this encyclopedia.

## Review Guide

This website documents the assumptions and calculations of an offshore wind infrastructure techno-economic model. It is a methodology draft for review.

Start with [System Boundary and Carrier-Cost Metrics](methodology/system_boundary_and_lcoe.qmd), followed by [Architecture Component Mapping](architectures/component_mapping.qmd), then a component calculation of interest.

Page readiness labels distinguish calculations that can be implemented from those with unresolved inputs or modelling decisions. A **blocked** page identifies a material gap preventing completion of its calculation; it may still contain usable calculation steps. Missing evidence is retained explicitly as a TODO.

Feedback is particularly welcome on system boundaries, calculation traceability, the suitability of modelling assumptions, and whether the level of detail is justified by the available evidence.
